findings.where: The full-width blue band straight after the hero, 'Get Mark's briefings on PPP reform' with its 'Subscribe' button (desktop-02 top; phone-01 directly under the email action)
findings.fault: A second call to action sits right under the hero, and it is louder than the first. It is a full-bleed field of the house blue with a heading bigger than the hero's own action, so it outweighs the 'Write to me directly' box in a squint. The button is a link to #subscribe, and the parts map shows no form or field anywhere on the page, so pressing it goes nowhere. It also offers a 'briefings' service the brief never mentions, and it speaks of Mark in the third person ('Mark's briefings') right after his first-person hero.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose brief asks for one message and one action, one direct way to reach Mark, and never an invented offering. A development-bank officer who presses Subscribe and gets nothing would be left wondering which route Mark actually wants them to use.

findings.fault: The v7 idea is Mark at work: a full-bleed photograph of him speaking. Here the lectern photo is keyed into a cut-out head and shoulders floating on flat slate. The event, the lectern and the room are gone, so it reads as a giant studio headshot. At this size the face looms over the page like a campaign poster rather than a working advisor seen at a talk.
findings.who_objects: The founder, who asked for 'Mark at work' as a direction distinct from v6's portrait. A visitor also loses the one cue that shows standing at a glance: Mark speaking at a named event.

findings.where: Article specimen: body paragraphs, the subhead and the three-item numbered list (desktop-04 to desktop-06; phone-03, phone-04)
findings.fault: The running article text is centred. Every line starts at a different place, so long paragraphs are hard to follow. In the list, the blue numbers hang at the left margin while each item's centred lines drift away from them, so item 2's text starts far from its '2.'.
findings.who_objects: The reader of Mark's articles (the brief calls the article the product) and Angélique, whose lists and paragraphs will all come out ragged on both sides.

findings.fault: There is no navigation: only the name and the logo. Nothing reaches Mark's articles, talks or background, and there is no 'Contact' item. The palette even lists 'nav links' as a use for mist, but none appear.
findings.who_objects: A procurement officer arriving from LinkedIn who wants his publications or CV before writing. The founder too, since the brief names nav as a part of the first screen.

findings.where: Lecture card at the end of the article specimen, 'Streamlining the PPP Process … PDF' (desktop-06; phone-04)
findings.fault: The card shows a download arrow and 'PDF', but its link goes to #article, an in-page anchor, not a file. It is also the only object on the page with rounded corners, a tinted blue fill, a blue border and a wide soft shadow together, while every other surface is square and flat.
findings.who_objects: A reader who presses it expecting the lecture's PDF and is taken to an anchor instead. The founder, because the one off-pattern card looks borrowed from a different site.

findings.where: Section labels below the fold: 'PALETTE', 'Type pair', 'Texture', 'An article page', 'Motion sketch' (desktop-02 to desktop-06)
findings.fault: Labels of the same rank get three different treatments: tracked blue capitals ('PALETTE'), a small bold grey sans ('Type pair', 'An article page', 'Motion sketch') and a large italic serif ('Texture'). 'PALETTE' also breaks the tile's own stated rules ('never tracked capitals'; 'blue only where something can be clicked'): it is blue but cannot be clicked.
findings.who_objects: The founder judging the tile, who sees the tile's own type rules broken inside the tile. Angélique too, since she has no single label style to copy.

findings.where: Article list numbers (desktop-05, phone-04), and the palette note that gives them to the house blue
findings.fault: The house blue marks links and the action, yet it also colours the list numbers, which cannot be clicked. That blurs what blue means on this page.
findings.who_objects: A reader scanning for links who sees blue numbers and wonders whether they act.

findings.where: Nav lockup, 'Mark M. Moseley' beside the MMM Infra mark (desktop-01, phone-01)
findings.fault: The name is set small and light, while the bolder mark beside it outweighs it, so the firm's logo wins over the name. Also, only the logo links home; the name, which visitors conventionally press to go home, does nothing.
findings.who_objects: The founder, whose personal-advisor test says his name leads with the logo beside it. A visitor who presses the name expecting home gets nothing.

findings.fault: The cut-out head is jammed between the logo and the heading. The logo's arches touch the crown of the head, and the first lines of the heading run over Mark's suit and chin, so name, face and line collide in the first 500 px.
findings.who_objects: A phone visitor, who gets a cramped, overlapping first screen instead of a calm one.

findings.fault: Nothing on the page says where Mark is based or which regions he has worked in, and the hero's claim to advise development banks and governments has no named work, event or place beside it.
findings.who_objects: A development-bank officer weighing him against terms of reference, who needs region and evidence of comparable work before writing.
